exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. PyTorch stable documentation reviewed 2026-09-19 (current docs identified as 2.14).

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; typed recall and coding questions provide the scored retrieval signal.

authoring_notes: This is a practical learning track, not a certification. Domain weights are curriculum emphasis weights used for adaptive selection. Learning placeholders are exact cloze versions of their revealed text. Reviewed against PyTorch 2.14-era official documentation and the app's structured typed-fill code/table renderer on 2026-09-19.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` creates a tensor from existing Python data, while factory functions such as `torch.zeros` and `torch.randn` create new tensor values.

reveal.text: `torch.tensor(...)` creates a tensor from existing Python data, while factory functions such as `torch.zeros` and `torch.randn` create new tensor values.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A common explicit constructor is `x = __________(data, dtype=torch.float32)`.

reveal.text: A common explicit constructor is `x = torch.tensor(data, dtype=torch.float32)`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not use `__________` when you only need another view or copy; tensor construction can copy data and lose autograd history.

reveal.text: Do not use `torch.tensor(existing_tensor)` when you only need another view or copy; tensor construction can copy data and lose autograd history.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` reports dimension sizes, `tensor.ndim` reports the number of dimensions, and `tensor.numel()` reports the total number of elements.

reveal.text: `tensor.shape` reports dimension sizes, `tensor.ndim` reports the number of dimensions, and `tensor.numel()` reports the total number of elements.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: For a batch tensor, `batch_size = __________` reads the leading dimension.

reveal.text: For a batch tensor, `batch_size = x.shape[0]` reads the leading dimension.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not confuse `__________` with `numel()`: one counts axes and the other counts elements.

reveal.text: Do not confuse `ndim` with `numel()`: one counts axes and the other counts elements.

source_refs.title: Shape, dimensions, and element count — PyTorch documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A tensor has a `dtype` and a `device`, and __________ can move it to another device or convert its dtype.

reveal.text: A tensor has a `dtype` and a `device`, and `.to(...)` can move it to another device or convert its dtype.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A common training pattern is `x = __________` before the forward pass.

reveal.text: A common training pattern is `x = x.to(device)` before the forward pass.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Model parameters and input tensors used by the same operation normally need to be on __________.

reveal.text: Model parameters and input tensors used by the same operation normally need to be on compatible devices.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` sets the seed for generating random numbers on all devices for PyTorch random-number generators.

reveal.text: `torch.manual_seed(seed)` sets the seed for generating random numbers on all devices for PyTorch random-number generators.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use a __________ when you want runs to begin from repeatable PyTorch random-number sequences.

reveal.text: Use a fixed seed when you want runs to begin from repeatable PyTorch random-number sequences.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A fixed seed improves reproducibility but __________ every operation is deterministic on every platform.

reveal.text: A fixed seed improves reproducibility but does not by itself guarantee every operation is deterministic on every platform.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ changes tensor shape while preserving the number of elements and may return either a view or a copy.

reveal.text: `reshape` changes tensor shape while preserving the number of elements and may return either a view or a copy.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use `__________` when one dimension should be inferred automatically.

reveal.text: Use `x.reshape(batch, -1)` when one dimension should be inferred automatically.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not depend on `reshape` __________; use shape semantics rather than copy-versus-view behavior as your assumption.

reveal.text: Do not depend on `reshape` returning a view; use shape semantics rather than copy-versus-view behavior as your assumption.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` inserts a size-1 dimension, while `squeeze(dim)` removes a size-1 dimension at the selected position.

reveal.text: `unsqueeze(dim)` inserts a size-1 dimension, while `squeeze(dim)` removes a size-1 dimension at the selected position.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use `__________` to add a leading batch-like axis to an unbatched tensor.

reveal.text: Use `x.unsqueeze(0)` to add a leading batch-like axis to an unbatched tensor.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Be careful with __________ when a batch dimension can equal 1, because it removes every size-1 dimension.

reveal.text: Be careful with bare `squeeze()` when a batch dimension can equal 1, because it removes every size-1 dimension.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ reorders multiple dimensions, while `transpose(dim0, dim1)` swaps two dimensions.

reveal.text: `permute(...)` reorders multiple dimensions, while `transpose(dim0, dim1)` swaps two dimensions.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Image pipelines often use `__________` to convert NHWC data to NCHW.

reveal.text: Image pipelines often use `x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2)` to convert NHWC data to NCHW.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Permuting dimensions __________ and layout; some later operations may require a compatible or contiguous layout.

reveal.text: Permuting dimensions changes strides and layout; some later operations may require a compatible or contiguous layout.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ joins tensors along an existing dimension, while `torch.stack` joins tensors along a newly created dimension.

reveal.text: `torch.cat` joins tensors along an existing dimension, while `torch.stack` joins tensors along a newly created dimension.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use `__________` when separate same-shaped samples should become a new batch dimension.

reveal.text: Use `torch.stack(samples, dim=0)` when separate same-shaped samples should become a new batch dimension.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not substitute `stack` for `cat`: `stack` __________ and `cat` does not.

reveal.text: Do not substitute `stack` for `cat`: `stack` increases the number of dimensions and `cat` does not.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ lets compatible tensor shapes participate in elementwise operations without explicitly copying values to the larger shape.

reveal.text: Broadcasting lets compatible tensor shapes participate in elementwise operations without explicitly copying values to the larger shape.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A bias shaped `[features]` can __________ a batch shaped `[batch, features]` during addition.

reveal.text: A bias shaped `[features]` can broadcast across a batch shaped `[batch, features]` during addition.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Two dimensions are not broadcast-compatible when their sizes differ and __________.

reveal.text: Two dimensions are not broadcast-compatible when their sizes differ and neither size is 1.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Reduction operations such as `sum` and `mean` reduce values along selected dimensions, and `__________` preserves reduced axes with size 1.

reveal.text: Reduction operations such as `sum` and `mean` reduce values along selected dimensions, and `keepdim=True` preserves reduced axes with size 1.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use `__________` to average across the first dimension.

reveal.text: Use `x.mean(dim=0)` to average across the first dimension.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Choosing the __________ is a common shape bug because it changes which axis is aggregated.

reveal.text: Choosing the wrong `dim` is a common shape bug because it changes which axis is aggregated.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ and the `@` operator perform matrix multiplication with PyTorch broadcasting rules for batched dimensions.

reveal.text: `torch.matmul` and the `@` operator perform matrix multiplication with PyTorch broadcasting rules for batched dimensions.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: For a linear-style calculation, `y = __________` multiplies feature vectors by transposed weight rows.

reveal.text: For a linear-style calculation, `y = x @ weight.T` multiplies feature vectors by transposed weight rows.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ is not matrix multiplication.

reveal.text: Elementwise `*` is not matrix multiplication.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ converts scores along a chosen dimension into values that sum to 1, while `argmax` returns the index of the largest value.

reveal.text: `softmax` converts scores along a chosen dimension into values that sum to 1, while `argmax` returns the index of the largest value.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: For class logits shaped `[batch, classes]`, class probabilities commonly use `softmax(logits, __________)`.

reveal.text: For class logits shaped `[batch, classes]`, class probabilities commonly use `softmax(logits, dim=1)`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ before `CrossEntropyLoss`; it expects unnormalized logits.

reveal.text: Do not apply softmax before `CrossEntropyLoss`; it expects unnormalized logits.
